subject: Cognitive Science
title: The Bottleneck Theory
description: A micro-lesson that makes The Bottleneck Theory usable.

hook.text: Flash two signals and ask for two responses. Even trained subjects can't process both at once.

buildup.text: Welford and Pashler found a central bottleneck: only one decision can occupy the processor at a time.

discovery.text: Perception and motor responses can overlap, but the decision stage is strictly single-threaded.

twist.text: This bottleneck persists even after years of practice. It appears hardwired, not trainable.

climax.text: It explains why texting and driving is dangerous: both require the same single decision channel.

punchline.text: Your brain can sense two things but decide only one.

quiz.question: What does bottleneck theory say is single-threaded?
